subject: Partner paper: clarify pass-through taxation & reseller glossary
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie@cloudcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partner paper: reseller pass-through questions

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the draft partner paper. Before we send this through procurement, our finance team has a couple of asks around the pass-through tax language and a short reseller glossary so our billing operations know how to treat marketplace transactions. Two quick items: 

1) The clause that says "customer is responsible for applicable taxes" — can we clarify whether that includes withholding in certain jurisdictions, or should that be an explicit carve-out?

2) We also need a one-paragraph definition in the partner paper that differentiates "Reseller" vs "Marketplace Seller" for downstream revenue flows.

I can loop in our counsel if you want redline suggestions, otherwise send us a version with suggested phrasing and we'll review. Attaching the partner paper your team sent for reference.

Thanks,
Ellie
Ellie Park
Head of Partnerships, CloudCart Inc
ellie@cloudcart.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper: reseller pass-through questions

Hi Ellie — thanks for the clear asks.

We reviewed this with Product and Revenue Ops and drafted two things for your review: a short reseller glossary paragraph and a tighter pass-through taxation paragraph that explicitly addresses withholding and cross-border VAT/GST. I attached a redline (RDW_CloudCart_PartnerPaper_v3_redline.docx) and a clean Order Form with billing flow callouts (OrderForm-CloudCart-2026-10-04.pdf).

High-level summary on our approach:
- Pass-through taxes: we propose that customers remain responsible for consumption taxes (VAT/GST/sales tax) and that any withholding required by the purchaser's jurisdiction will be treated as a tax for which the purchaser is responsible; Redwood will provide documentation of gross invoice amounts and tax credits where applicable.
- Withholding carve-outs: we are reluctant to accept a broad indemnity for withholding unless there is clear conduit/collection responsibility. We propose a limited cooperation clause (see redline).

Can you confirm whether CloudCart prefers the purchaser to handle withholding or if you want Redwood to gross-up amounts? If you prefer a gross-up, we'll need sign-off from Finance and Sales leadership (Ben copied).

Next steps: Ben — can you review the proposed language re: gross-up vs purchaser withholding? Marissa — please advise on the proposed legal language.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper: reseller pass-through questions

Thanks Monica. Quick commercial note from Sales: CloudCart wants the option to route customer payments through their marketplace and have Redwood invoice CloudCart for a wholesale price (standard marketplace flow). If CloudCart is invoicing end customers and is responsible for local withholding, they will expect Redwood to accept net-of-withholding payments.

Proposed compromise (commercial): If withholding is required by law at the customer jurisdiction and CloudCart provides a valid tax withholding certificate, Redwood will accept net payment but reserves the right to request gross-up for any amounts where the withholding causes material shortfall relative to the agreed fees.

Please see inline suggested text for the partner paper (below):

"If applicable law requires the Customer to withhold or deduct taxes from payments to Redwood, Customer shall provide Redwood with official documentation of the withholding and remit the balance to Redwood. Where withholding reduces the net payment below the agreed amount, Customer shall either (a) gross-up the payment to make Redwood whole, or (b) obtain Redwood's prior written consent to accept the net-of-withholding amount. Redwood may request reasonable documentation to substantiate withholding amounts."

Marissa — any issues with that from a legal risk perspective? We want something operationally straightforward for CloudCart.

- Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper: reseller pass-through questions

Ben / Monica — thanks for the draft. Legal thoughts below.

1) Withholding/gross-up text: the language Ben proposed is generally acceptable but we should add a timebox and documentation requirements to limit exposure. Suggested tweak: 

"If applicable law requires withholding, the Customer shall (i) provide Redwood with official withholding documentation within thirty (30) days of payment; (ii) promptly remit any additional gross-up amount required to make Redwood whole; and (iii) permit Redwood to request reasonable evidence of the withholding tax computation. Redwood may require a gross-up where withholding reduces the net payment to an amount that materially impacts Redwood's fee economics (e.g., >5% shortfall)."

2) Reseller glossary: propose short definitions to avoid downstream confusion. Add to partner paper under Definitions: 
- "Reseller": an entity that purchases Redwood services from the Partner for resale to End Customers and is invoiced directly by Redwood or Redwood's designated billing agent.
- "Marketplace Seller": an End Customer listing and selling through Partner's marketplace where Partner collects payments from End Customers and remits amounts to Redwood under the Partner's reseller arrangement.

3) Indemnity and data residency: Don't expand indemnities for tax beyond cooperation and documentation. Keep Redwood's obligations limited and require Partner to use commercially reasonable efforts to collect and remit. If CloudCart insists on broader indemnity, we should require a capped exposure or carve-out for third-party taxes.

4) Operational items: include an attachment checklist for required tax certificates, evidence types, and the contact where CloudCart should send withholding documentation (finance-tax@redwood.com).

I've added tracked redline language in the attached RDW_CloudCart_PartnerPaper_v3_redline.docx. If CloudCart's counsel needs to propose alternate wording, we can review but we should avoid open-ended gross-up commitments without Finance sign-off.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Counsel, Contracts & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: 2026-10-05T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper: reseller pass-through questions — redline and DocuSign

Monica / Ellie — reviewed the redline this morning. High-level: CloudCart is generally comfortable with the documentation + materiality compromise, but we have two narrow asks: 

1) For certain LATAM and EMEA customers, tax authorities can require withholdings that are effectively irreversible for the seller. In those cases, CloudCart asks Redwood to accept a listed-country exception where gross-up is not required but the parties will use the attached mitigation checklist and close the tax credit loop. We provided a short annex suggestion (see attached commentary).

2) A small change to the Definitions: we recommend replacing "invoiced directly by Redwood" with "invoiced by Redwood or Redwood's designated billing agent" to allow the marketplace-facilitated billing flow.

If Redwood accepts the annex approach, we can sign the partner paper with an annex listing the agreed jurisdictions where gross-up is not mandated and a process for monthly reconciliation. Otherwise CloudCart would need a parent-level indemnity for third-party tax in those countries, which is commercially challenging for them.

I've uploaded our markup and a short annex draft to the DocuSign envelope you shared. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the annex approach or if you need further finance-level discussion.

Regards,
Sam Lee
Harrington LLP — International Tax & Commercial Counsel
sam.lee@harrington-llp.com
